en.question: Prompt caching is enabled with a cache breakpoint after a 12,000-token reference document. On the second identical request within the cache lifetime, what is the billing effect for that prefix?

options.text: It is charged again at the standard base input rate for that model.
options.note: That is the behaviour without caching, or when the prefix has changed.

options.text: It is charged at the reduced cache-read rate, roughly a tenth of base input.
It is charged as output tokens because it is replayed into the response.
options.note: Cached content is input and is never reclassified as output.

options.text: It is supplied entirely free of charge for the lifetime of the cache entry.
options.note: Reads are heavily discounted but they are not free.

en.explanation: A hit bills the reused prefix at roughly 0.1x base input. The first request pays a write premium above base input, so caching pays off once a stable prefix is reused several times.
